question: v09
q: Has eating out got more expensive in Melbourne?

transcript.answer:
Yes. Eating out in Melbourne keeps getting more expensive. Prices are still rising, though a little more slowly than a few months ago and a bit more slowly than in the rest of the country.

**Latest figure (August 2026):** "Meals out and takeaway foods" prices in Melbourne were **3.5% higher than a year earlier** (ABS monthly CPI). Melbourne's overall inflation was also **3.5%**, so restaurant and takeaway prices rose about as fast as everything else.

**Recent trend (year-on-year change, Melbourne):**
| Period | Meals out & takeaway | All items |
|---|---|---|
| Apr 2025 | 2.6% | 2.3% |
| Aug 2025 | 3.4% | 2.5% |
| Jan 2026 | 3.8% | 3.3% |
| May 2026 | **4.4%** (peak) | 3.5% |
| Jul 2026 | 4.1% | 3.2% |
| Aug 2026 | 3.5% | 3.5% |

- From early 2025 the annual rate climbed from about 2.5% to a peak of 4.4% in May 2026. It has eased since then, down to 3.5% in August.
- **Longer view:** the quarterly CPI shows the rate was even higher in early 2024, at **5.8%** in the March quarter. It cooled to about 2.3–2.7% through the first half of 2025 before picking up again. These are yearly growth rates, so they add up: prices are well above where they were two or three years ago, not just slightly up on last year.

**Compared with the rest of Australia:** across the eight capitals, meals out and takeaway prices rose **4.1%** in the year to August 2026, so Melbourne is currently a bit below the national rate.

**In short:** eating out in Melbourne cost about 3.5% more in August 2026 than a year earlier. That's down from 4.4% in May, and in recent months it has risen at or above Melbourne's overall inflation rate.
